title: Agentforce Pricing 2026: Plans and Costs Explained
summary: Agentforce pricing ranges from $5 to $550 per user monthly depending on your plan choice. See the full breakdown and determine which tier fits your budget.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces for agents that work across non-Salesforce apps


Activepieces fits when the agent's job spans apps outside Salesforce, because its core is MIT-licensed and you can self-host it, which limits the rebuild cost that vendor-hosted agents carry.


### When the job lives outside Salesforce


Take an agent that reads a support email, checks an order in a billing tool, drafts a reply and logs the result in a spreadsheet.


Nothing in that job touches Salesforce data, so paying for Agentforce's conversation or action metering and the licences underneath it buys capability you never use.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pricing) builds this as a flow with an AI agent step, and that step can call any of its 741 integrations, which the project calls[pieces](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces) .


The agent's reach is therefore the connector list, not one vendor's data model, so check that your apps are on it before you commit.


Where Agentforce counts conversations or actions, Activepieces meters usage in credits, and its free plan includes 1,000 credits a month with unlimited flows. That's a different unit, so you can't compare sticker prices.


Take your expected runs per month, multiply by the steps each run triggers, and set that against the free plan's 1,000 monthly credits and the $20-a-month Plus plan, as listed on Activepieces' own pricing page on 2026-10-12, rather than trusting a figure quoted second-hand.


If you want to test the model on a real workflow, you can[try it free](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_body&ref=%2Fblog%2Fagentforce-pricing-2026-plans-and-costs-explained) .


### Agentforce approval steps and self-hosting options


Before the agent acts, a flow can pause for a human to approve. For anything that sends money, email or customer-facing text, that pause turns a runaway agent into a queued request, and it keeps a person accountable for the action.


Self-hosting is the lock-in answer. Because the code is open source and runs on your infrastructure, no vendor's servers hold your flows.


The trade-off is that you now carry the hosting, upgrades and uptime, which is a staffing cost to put in the same spreadsheet as the licence line.


If the agent's work is mostly Salesforce-native, such as reading and updating cases, opportunities or Data Cloud records under your existing permission model, Agentforce sits closest to that data.


Activepieces would reach it through its Salesforce connector, with access governed by RBAC, centrally held credentials and project isolation, and audit logs recording what the agent did (RBAC and audit logs are Enterprise Edition features).


In that case a licence premium, such as the $12,500 a month the 100-seat core add-on costs, may be cheaper than the integration work.
